newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen easing as momentum turns lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen easing as momentum turns lower.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Cocoa futures are expected to edge lower as the overall technical picture turns more bearish and the key July contract slides towards nearby support levels, analysts and traders said on Wednesday.
Traders called the market to open three stg lower than Tuesday's July close of 1,017 stg, adding that the close, which was down nine on the day, was not particularly positive.
July's close should provide a path for a test of support at 1,000, they said.
Technical analysts said while the contract had been struggling to claw its way back to the April peaks at 1,065 and 1,061, rallies tended to run into persistent selling.
This suggested a more bearish scenario, especially as the last three closes were mid-range and not near intra-day highs, they said.
July's short-term momentum indicators, based over periods of five and 10 days, are sliding away from positive territory towards zero -- suggesting a more bearish tone for the market.
"It's going sideways and has got resistance at the peak areas just above 1,060," said Susan Rigg, a technical analyst at Chart Analysis.
"The way it's moving up is not nearly as dramatic as the way it's moving down."
For an immediate upside target, July would have to approach and preferably conquer the 1,046 high scored at the end of last week to indicate that the market tone was still bullish.
"It's got to have a look at that peak we saw in late May to say we've got a chance of going up," Rigg said.
"I would have thought it's more likely to come back and look at the 980 area -- and if that breaks it's going to be bad news."
